# Results — Study 592 (Dual Momentum — GEM)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test
(Antonacci 2012/2014) — **Global Equities Momentum: 12-month absolute + relative momentum on
US vs international equities, bonds when both fail the T-bill hurdle, beats buy-and-hold with
half the drawdown** — rebuilt on the live-ETF tape (SPY / EFA / AGG with an IEF splice / ^IRX).
Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.
As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete month; the partial current month is dropped; run date
2026-07-03). Fingerprint `837a69932f70`.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily auto-adjusted (total-return) closes: **SPY**, **EFA**, **AGG**, **IEF** + **^IRX** (13-week T-bill yield) — public, no key |
| Window | **2002-09-30 → 2026-06-30** (286 months, **23.8 years**; starts at EFA's first full 12-month formation window) |
| Bond leg | AGG's monthly return, **IEF-spliced** before AGG's first monthly return (Sept 2003) — documented |
| Risk-free | ^IRX yield observed at the **end of the prior month** / 12 — known in advance, no look-ahead |
| Rules | Antonacci's tree at each month-end: if SPY's trailing 12-m return > cumulated T-bill return, hold the better of SPY/EFA by 12-m return; else hold bonds |
| Execution / costs | signal from month-end closes, position earns the **following** month — exactly **one** one-month decision-to-earn lag; **5 / 10 / 20 bps** one-way × NAV per traded leg, 2 legs per switch; long-only, no borrow |
| Allocation | SPY **50.0%** / EFA **31.1%** / BOND **18.9%** of months; **35 switches** (1.47/yr) |
| Survivorship | none — broad index ETFs, not a picked panel. The honest caveat is instead **sample start**: the live-ETF tape begins 2002; Antonacci's celebrated 1974→2011 backtest years are *not* observable here |

## Headline — GEM vs SPY buy-and-hold vs 60/40 (gross, total-return, same 286 months)

| leg | CAGR | ann. vol | Sharpe (excess) | max DD |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **GEM** | **+9.87%** | 12.15% | 0.70 | **−20.7%** |
| SPY buy-and-hold | +11.22% | 14.77% | 0.68 | −50.8% |
| 60/40 (SPY/AGG, monthly rebal.) | +8.27% | 9.34% | **0.72** | −32.3% |

| active return | bps/mo | %/yr | HAC t |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| GEM − SPY | −13.3 | **−1.59** | **−0.64** |
| GEM − 60/40 | +14.8 | +1.77 | +0.89 |

The claim splits cleanly in two. **"Half the drawdown" is on the tape**: GEM's max drawdown is
−20.7% vs SPY's −50.8% — a ratio of **0.41**, better than half. **"Beats buy-and-hold" is
not**: GEM *lags* SPY by 1.59%/yr (HAC t = −0.64), and its excess-vs-excess Sharpe (0.70) is
statistically indistinguishable from SPY's (0.68) — and *below* a plain no-timing 60/40's
(0.72). Sharpe races are excess-of-T-bill on both sides; all legs total-return.

## Costs — cheap to run, but costs are not the problem

One-way bps × NAV per traded leg (2 legs per switch, 1 initial entry); benchmarks gross.

| one-way cost | GEM net CAGR | net Sharpe | active vs SPY | HAC t |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5 bps | +9.71% | 0.69 | −1.74%/yr | −0.70 |
| 10 bps | +9.54% | 0.68 | −1.89%/yr | −0.75 |
| 20 bps | +9.22% | 0.65 | −2.19%/yr | −0.86 |

At 1.47 switches/yr the cost drag is ~3–16 bps/yr — negligible. The shortfall vs buy-and-hold
is the *signal's* doing, not friction's.

## Lookback placebo grid — is 12 months special, or lucky?

Same engine, same months (common start), only the formation window moves.

| lookback | CAGR | Sharpe | max DD | active vs SPY | HAC t |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 3 m | +10.46% | 0.80 | −19.2% | −1.18%/yr | −0.52 |
| 6 m | +8.97% | 0.66 | −24.9% | −2.49%/yr | −0.95 |
| 9 m | +8.79% | 0.64 | −20.1% | −2.65%/yr | −1.06 |
| **12 m (canonical)** | +9.87% | 0.70 | −20.7% | **−1.59%/yr** | **−0.64** |

**No lookback beats buy-and-hold** on this tape — 12 is neither special nor lucky; the whole
grid lags SPY. (12 m is second-best in the grid, so the canonical choice isn't cherry-picked
against; there is simply no positive active return to find.)

## Random-switching baseline — 40 seeds, averaged (single-seed baselines are banned)

Each seed permutes GEM's **own** monthly holdings — same assets, same time-in-market
(50/31/19), random *timing* — isolating whether GEM's switch dates carry information.

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| mean Welch t (GEM vs shuffled months), 40 seeds | **+0.26** |
| shuffled-timing baseline mean CAGR / Sharpe | +8.53% / 0.54 |
| share of shuffles GEM's CAGR beats | 77.5% |

GEM's timing is *better than random* (it beats ~78% of shuffles and adds ~1.3 pp CAGR over
them) — that is the drawdown-avoidance mechanism working — but the averaged Welch t of **0.26**
is nowhere near significance. Timing skill exists in the point estimate, not at the bar.

## Sub-periods — does it live off 2008 alone? Yes.

| window | GEM CAGR / DD / Sharpe | SPY CAGR / DD / Sharpe | active | HAC t |
|---|---|---|--:|--:|
| full sample | +9.87% / −20.7% / 0.70 | +11.22% / −50.8% / 0.68 | −1.59%/yr | −0.64 |
| **ex-GFC** (drop 2007-07 → 2009-06) | +11.00% / −20.7% / 0.78 | +14.62% / −23.9% / 0.95 | **−3.43%/yr** | **−2.02** |
| 2010 → | +8.57% / −20.7% / 0.59 | +14.23% / −23.9% / 0.90 | −5.32%/yr | −3.37 |
| pre-2013 | +10.80% / −17.3% / 0.79 | +6.46% / −50.8% / 0.38 | +3.53%/yr | +0.71 |
| post-2013 | +9.16% / −20.7% / 0.63 | +15.01% / −23.9% / 0.94 | **−5.51%/yr** | **−2.96** |

Remove the two GFC years and GEM's underperformance turns **statistically significant**
(−3.43%/yr, HAC t = −2.02). From 2010 on it is −5.32%/yr (t = −3.37). The entire case for GEM
on the live-ETF tape is one great sidestep: 2008.

## Third axis — has GEM decayed since publication (2013)?

Antonacci's *Risk Premia Harvesting* paper circulated 2012–2013; the *Dual Momentum Investing*
book followed in 2014. Split at 2013-01 (a justified, pre-registered publication split — not
snooped):

| period | active vs SPY | HAC t |
|---|--:|--:|
| pre-2013 (n = 124) | **+29.4 bps/mo** | +0.71 |
| post-2013 (n = 162) | **−45.9 bps/mo** | **−2.96** |
| Welch t of the pre-vs-post difference | | **+2.02** |

The difference clears the bar (Welch t = 2.02): post-publication GEM flipped from mildly
positive (never significant) to **significantly negative** active returns — whipsawed in
2015-16, out for the v-shaped 2020 recovery, and lagging the 2023-25 US bull. **Decay
CONFIRMED.**

## Synthetic machinery control — the engine is faithful

A two-state bull/bear Markov world where the knob is regime **persistence**; the unconditional
equity premium over bonds is positive in both worlds, so only *timing* can win. 80 years
monthly, deterministic seed.

| world | active vs buy-and-hold | HAC t | max DD GEM vs B&H |
|---|--:|--:|---|
| **null** (i.i.d. regimes — no information in past returns) | −1.58%/yr | **−1.24** | −37% vs −61% |
| **planted** (persistence 0.94 — multi-year trends) | +4.67%/yr | **+2.86** | −28% vs −93% |

With no planted trend the engine does **not** manufacture outperformance (it pays the timing
drag, exactly as theory predicts); with genuinely persistent regimes it lights up at t = 2.86
and slashes the drawdown. The machinery can detect the effect when it exists — so the flat/
negative real-tape reading is a property of the tape, not of the harness. *(A faithful-engine /
power check only — never cited in support of a stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — MIXED** (*Real on the drawdown-halving · None on the beats-buy-and-hold*). The
  half-the-drawdown leg is on the tape: **−20.7% vs −50.8%** (ratio 0.41), the mechanical
  consequence of spending 19% of months in bonds after down-trends. The outperformance leg is
  not: active vs SPY is **−1.59%/yr (HAC t = −0.64)** full-sample, **significantly negative**
  once the GFC is excluded (t = −2.02) and post-2013 (t = −2.96); no lookback in the 3/6/9/12
  grid beats buy-and-hold; the 40-seed random-switching Welch t averages **+0.26**. No
  survivorship (index ETFs) — but the live-ETF sample starts 2002 and cannot see the 1974-2011
  years the book's backtest is built on.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Not for costs (1.47 switches/yr ≈ 3–16 bps/yr, capacity effectively
  unlimited, three of the most liquid ETFs on earth — execution is trivial) but because the
  product being sold doesn't exist on the deployable tape: since publication GEM has *cost*
  −5.51%/yr vs SPY (t = −2.96), and its full-sample risk-adjusted profile (Sharpe 0.70) is
  matched by a no-timing 60/40 (0.72) with a similar drawdown philosophy. The accessible,
  cheap-to-run wrapper delivers beta plus a 2008 story — the promised alpha is a mirage.
- **Decayed since publication (2013)? — CONFIRMED.** Pre-2013 +29.4 bps/mo (t = +0.71,
  never significant) vs post-2013 **−45.9 bps/mo (t = −2.96)**; the pre-vs-post difference
  clears the bar at Welch t = **+2.02**.
